result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse (new file), the function returns `refreshTokenResponse` — the full safeParse wrapper ({success, data, error}), not `.data`. Google CalendarService stores this directly: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ ... data: { key } })`. So credential.key persists the wrapper object, and on next load `token.access_token`/`expiry_date` reads via the wrapper shape fail (key is not the parsed credential object), breaking refresh until re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential is now computed as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not `result.data`. This means the stored `credential.key` becomes the wrapper object, so later code expecting `credential.key.access_token`/`expiry_date` will get `undefined`, matching the reported breakage after first refresh.
